entries.implementation_notes: [repo=legacy-law-identity] Consolidated the 15 approved sidenote-extraction corrections into 5 changes in resolver.py. (1) Public resolutions: added _RES_RE to detect '[Pub. Res., No. N]' and OCR variants ('Public. Res.', missing 'No.', stray commas/periods/spaces) from the flattened sidenote text; these resolve directly to the distinct 'Public Resolution {congress}-{N}' identifier (is_public True) and are excluded from the public-act blank-fill so they neither drop nor perturb act numbering. (2) Comma tolerance: _PUBNO_RE now allows an OCR comma after 'No' (No[.,]?) so 'Public, No, N' extracts N. (3) Leading word-boundary: _PL_RE dropped the leading \b (now 'Public\s+Law\s+(\d+)') so a concatenated preceding bill ref ('...2422Public Law 799') still parses. (4) Alphabetic suffix: a lone trailing capital letter after the number (optionally hyphen/en/em-dash or one space, and NOT the first letter of a following word) is captured -> '{congress}-160A'. (5) Fractional suffix: a vulgar-fraction glyph immediately after the number (e.g. '297½') is preserved -> '74-297½'. Refactored the resolver to tag each record as act/resolution and run the monotonic blank-fill over act-only records, keeping the two-pass structure, blank-fill fallback, and normal 'Public Law N' -> '{congress}-{N}' behavior unchanged; _sidenote_pl_number still returns the base act int (None for resolutions/'Pub. No.'). Every returned identifier retains a \d+[-–—]\d+ substring. Added 7 regression tests (Pub. Res., interleaved-act-numbering guard, comma-after-No, concatenated ref, -A suffix, over-match guard, fractional ½). Full suite: 23 passed.
